1.contenido: Canon 1 If anyone denies the one true God, Creator and Lord of things visible and invisible: let him be anathema.

2.contenido: Canon 2 If anyone is not ashamed to affirm that there is nothing outside matter: let him be anathema.

3.contenido: Sessio 3 Caput 4 This has also maintained and maintains the perpetual consensus of the Catholic Church: that there is a double order of knowledge, distinct not only by the principle, but also by the object: by the beginning, because in one we know by natural reason, in the other by divine faith; for the object, because in addition to those things that natural reason can reach, we are proposed to believe mysteries hidden in God, which, if they are not divinely revealed, cannot be made known.

4.contenido: Session 4 The eternal Shepherd and bishop of our souls, to make the saving work of redemption perennial, decreed to build the holy Church, in which, as in the house of the living God, all the faithful would be contained by the bond of a single faith and charity. Therefore, before being glorified, he prayed to the Father not only for the Apostles, but also for those who were to believe in him through their word, that they might all be one, just as the Son and the Father are one.

5.contenido: Canon 5 If anyone does not confess that the world and all the things contained in it, both spiritual and material, according to their entire substance, were produced by God out of nothing: let him be anathema.

6.contenido: Canon 6 If anyone says that the one true God, our Creator and Lord, cannot be known with certainty by the natural light of human reason through the things that have been made: let him be anathema.
